clauses.label: operative lead
clauses.text:
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the
laws of the United States of America, and in order to more accurately
describe the expertise requirements for members selected for the National
Bioethics Advisory Commission, it is hereby ordered that Executive Order
12975, as amended (‘‘Order’’), is further amended as follows:

clauses.label: Section 1.
clauses.text:
Section 1. Section 3 of the order shall read as follows: ‘‘ Sec. 3. Establishment
of National Bioethics Advisory Commission. There is established in the
Department of Health and Human Services a National Bioethics Advisory
Commission (NBAC). The NBAC shall be subject to the Federal Advisory
Committee Act, as amended (5 U.S.C. App.).’’

clauses.label: Sec. 2.
clauses.text:
Sec. 2. A new section 4 shall be added to the order to read: ‘‘ Sec. 4.
Structure. (a) The National Bioethics Advisory Commission shall be com-
posed of not more than 18 nongovernment members appointed by the Presi-
dent. At least one member shall be selected from each of the following
categories of primary expertise: (1) philosophy/theology; (2) social/behavioral
science; (3) law; (4) medicine/allied health professions; and (5) biological
research. At least three members shall be selected from the general public,
bringing to the Commission expertise other than that listed. The membership
shall be approximately evenly balanced between scientists and non-scientists.
Close attention will be given to equitable geographic distribution and to
ethnic and gender representation.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text:
(b) Members of the Commission will serve for terms of 2 years and
may continue to serve after the expiration of their term until a successor
is appointed. A member appointed to fill an unexpired term will be appointed
to the remainder of such term.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text:
(c) The President shall designate a Chairperson from among the members
of the NBAC.’’

clauses.label: Sec. 3.
clauses.text:
Sec. 3. (a) ‘‘[S]ection 5’’ in the third sentence of section 1(b) of the order
shall be deleted and ‘‘section 6’’ shall be inserted in lieu thereof.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text:
(b) Current sections 4 through 7 of Executive Order 12975 shall be renum-
bered sections 5 through 8.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text:
(c) New section 8(b) is amended by deleting ‘‘October 3, 1999’’ and insert-
ing ‘‘October 3, 2001’’ in lieu thereof.
œ–

Executive Order 13137 of September 15, 1999
Amendment to Executive Order 12975, as Amended, National
Bioethics Advisory Commission
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the
laws of the United States of America, and in order to more accurately
describe the expertise requirements for members selected for the National
Bioethics Advisory Commission, it is hereby ordered that Executive Order
12975, as amended (‘‘Order’’), is further amended as follows:
Section 1. Section 3 of the order shall read as follows: ‘‘ Sec. 3. Establishment
of National Bioethics Advisory Commission. There is established in the
Department of Health and Human Services a National Bioethics Advisory
Commission (NBAC). The NBAC shall be subject to the Federal Advisory
Committee Act, as amended (5 U.S.C. App.).’’
Sec. 2. A new section 4 shall be added to the order to read: ‘‘ Sec. 4.
Structure. (a) The National Bioethics Advisory Commission shall be com-
posed of not more than 18 nongovernment members appointed by the Presi-
dent. At least one member shall be selected from each of the following
categories of primary expertise: (1) philosophy/theology; (2) social/behavioral
science; (3) law; (4) medicine/allied health professions; and (5) biological
research. At least three members shall be selected from the general public,
bringing to the Commission expertise other than that listed. The membership
shall be approximately evenly balanced between scientists and non-scientists.
Close attention will be given to equitable geographic distribution and to
ethnic and gender representation.
(b) Members of the Commission will serve for terms of 2 years and
may continue to serve after the expiration of their term until a successor
is appointed. A member appointed to fill an unexpired term will be appointed
to the remainder of such term.
(c) The President shall designate a Chairperson from among the members
of the NBAC.’’
Sec. 3. (a) ‘‘[S]ection 5’’ in the third sentence of section 1(b) of the order
shall be deleted and ‘‘section 6’’ shall be inserted in lieu thereof.
(b) Current sections 4 through 7 of Executive Order 12975 shall be renum-
bered sections 5 through 8.
(c) New section 8(b) is amended by deleting ‘‘October 3, 1999’’ and insert-
ing ‘‘October 3, 2001’’ in lieu thereof.
œ–
THE WHITE HOUSE,
September 15, 1999.
[FR Doc. 99–24582
Filed 9–17–99; 8:45 am]

status_research.rationale: I read the complete held EO 13137 (64 FR 50733, Sept. 15, 1999): a pure amending order that rewrites sec. 3 of EO 12975, adds a new sec. 4 (membership/terms) and renumbers and amends sec. 8(b) (termination date moved from Oct. 3, 1999 to Oct. 3, 2001). Its operative effect exists only as amendments to the National Bioethics Advisory Commission order EO 12975. I also read the complete held EO 13316 (68 FR 55255, Sept. 17, 2003). Its Sec. 3(b) revokes, in a list of orders 'which established committees that have terminated or whose work is completed', 'Executive Order 12975, as amended by Executive Orders 13018, 13046, and 13137, establishing the National Bioethics Advisory Commission', expressly naming EO 13137 as part of the revoked instrument; Sec. 6 makes the order effective Sept. 30, 2003. Revoking the amended base order as amended by 13137 removes the only text 13137 amended, so no operative content of 13137 remains in force; nothing in EO 13316 saves any part of 13137 and the original 13137 has no independent continuing command, so no savings clause or partial scope applies. The only history observation (API catalog note 'Amends: EO 12975 / See: EO 13316') and its cross-reference candidate event agree with the held acting text but are editorial leads, not the basis. Earlier endings: EO 13137 sec. 3(c) moved the Commission's own termination to Oct. 3, 2001, so the Commission may have lapsed before 13316 (EO 12975 text not examined here); that would only move the end earlier and cannot make the order current at 2026-10-14. I do not assert the first-end date, which stays a lifecycle gap, nor any status through intervening periods. This is a provisional NO hypothesis only.

versions.research_rationale:
EO 13137 (signed 1999-09-15; 64 FR 50733, Federal Register of 1999-09-20, FR Doc. 99-24582) was read in full in the held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13137.txt. It further amends EO 12975 (National Bioethics Advisory Commission): section 1 restates section 3 of the parent, section 2 adds a new section 4 (membership of not more than 18, member terms and a Chairperson), and section 3 corrects a cross-reference, renumbers sections 4 through 7 as 5 through 8 and changes the termination date in new section 8(b) from October 3, 1999 to October 3, 2001. First end for every clause: EO 13316 (signed 2003-09-17; 68 FR 55255, Federal Register of 2003-09-23), section 3(b), revokes "Executive Order 12975, as amended by Executive Orders 13018, 13046," and 13137, establishing the Commission; section 6 states "This order shall be effective September 30, 2003." EO 13316 names this order. The restated termination date of October 3, 2001 is an earlier candidate: no held source shows an extension or the date the Commission actually ceased, so under the owner's 2026-10-21 reasoning (the order stays on the books until revoked) it is disclosed as a spent fact and not recorded as the end. The held text is the machine-extracted text layer of the official Federal Register PDF; the PDF page images are not held, so identity (printed number, title, signing date and FR Doc. number) was checked on the text layer against the census register row.
